Quick triage from Reliability:
- Initial telemetry (prefix-stats-20270809.csv) shows abnormal KV cache miss amplification on popular prefixes, causing repeated backend recomputation and elevated latencies.
- Autoscaler in us-west-2 did not fully trigger due to a mis-evaluated health metric (edge probe failing intermittently).
- Impact scope: primarily us-west-2; we see small ripple in us-east at low percentage. Not platform-wide yet.

Immediate mitigation plan (T-60 minutes target):
1) Force scale +2 worker pools in us-west-2 (Rohan) — provisioning started now.
2) Temporarily enable prefix-level KV caching for HighWater routes only (Aditya) — reduces recompute.
3) Route a subset of HighWater traffic to fallback quantized model variant that is compatible with existing prefix cache (Hannah).
4) Turn on short-term request-level circuit breaker at 3 rps for non-critical routes to reduce contention.

I will own technical updates and confirm when scaling completes. ETA: scaling + routing changes should yield measurable improvement in 30–45 minutes; full normalization expected 60–90 minutes depending on cache warmup.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachment: prefix-stats-20270809.csv (CSV, 12KB)

Elena —

Quick status update and short note for your ops/account teams. Key items: 
- Impact: Elevated error rate (502/504) and increased latency for /generate for a subset of HighWater traffic routed through us-west-2.
- Scope: Primarily us-west-2; we are not seeing a global platform outage.
- Root cause (interim): KV cache miss amplification combined with an autoscaler probe edge-case — triggers increased backend recompute and transient overload.
- Actions taken: +2 worker pools provisioned in us-west-2; prefix-level KV caching enabled for your routes; a portion of your traffic routed to the fallback quantized model to lower compute. Circuit breakers applied to non-critical routes.
- ETA: We observed improvement within ~35 minutes; target for full normalization 60–90 minutes as caches warm and traffic stabilizes.

Suggested customer-facing note (please feel free to reuse):
"Redwood is currently investigating elevated errors and latency affecting the /generate endpoint for some HighWater tenants in the us-west-2 region. Our team has applied targeted mitigations (additional capacity, route-level caching, and temporary fallback model routing). We expect progressive improvement over the next 60–90 minutes and will provide an update when service is fully restored. If you continue to see failures, please escalate to support@highwater.ai with request ids"

Next steps for Redwood: post-incident RCA and a proposed change to autoscaler health evaluation (Hannah/Platform) and follow-up with HighWater on permanent mitigations.

I’ll send a short executive summary for SLT now.
